items.title: Rossano Sportiello interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Hartford, New York, October 2, 2015 [interview 1 of 2]
items.q: I took a recording of Zoot Sims with a quartet because I wanted the saxophone player to hear that kind of playing.

ctx.x: Yeah and I don’t think the education system helps that that much. Over the years I’ve gone to some of the conferences, the jazz education conferences. And they have next to no what we might call traditional jazz being performed. And sometimes the students feel that the history of the saxophone started with John Coltrane, which is a shame.

Well when I was in Milan I was teaching also. I was in a jazz conservatory for seven years. And I remember that once one of my ensemble classes I took a recording of Zoot Sims with a quartet because I wanted the saxophone player to hear that kind of playing. And I was surprised that no one in the class ever heard of Zoot Sims.
I’m wondering about, people ask often, what are you thinking about when you improvise?
